provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Ready for primary school
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state changes in primary one.
The pupils should be able to ask questions about primary school.
Introduction:
We are big children now. We will soon go to primary one.
Content:
Primary one has big children. No more nap time. We carry big bags. We have many books. We sit on long benches. Teachers give homework. We make new friends.
Class activity:
Let's play 'Ask me about primary one'. I will point to a pupil and ask a question.
Evaluation questions:
What is different in primary one?
Who will teach you in primary one?
What do you want to know about primary one?
Summary:
We are ready for big school changes.

topics.title: Self care mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to dress themselves.
The pupils should be able to pack their school bags.
Introduction:
We are growing up fast. We must learn to do things alone.
Content:
Tie your shoes alone. Button your shirt. Pack your bag with your books and pencil. Put your water bottle inside. Check your bag every morning.
Class activity:
Let's practice packing our bags. Each pupil will pack their own bag.
Evaluation questions:
What should you pack in your bag?
How do you tie your shoes?
What do you do before leaving home?
Summary:
We can take care of ourselves now.

topics.title: Time management
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state their morning routine.
The pupils should be able to follow a timetable.
Introduction:
Time waits for no one. We must learn to use our time well.
Content:
Wake up early. Brush your teeth. Eat your breakfast. Put on your uniform. Carry your bag. Go to school on time. Use a timetable for your activities.
Class activity:
Let's make a picture timetable for our morning routine.
Evaluation questions:
What time do you wake up?
What comes first in your morning?
How does a timetable help us?
Summary:
Using time well makes us good children.

topics.title: Study habits
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify a good study place.
The pupils should be able to state when they study best.
Introduction:
Learning is important. We need good places to learn.
Content:
Find a quiet place. Sit at a table. Use good light. Keep your books neat. Study when you are not tired. Your study corner should have no toys. Only books and pencils.
Class activity:
Let's draw our perfect study corner.
Evaluation questions:
Where do you study best?
What makes a good study place?
When do you like to study?
Summary:
Good study habits help us learn more.

topics.title: Speaking up
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to ask questions in class.
The pupils should be able to show and tell something.
Introduction:
We have good ideas. We must learn to share them.
Content:
Raise your hand to speak. Speak clearly. Look at the teacher. Ask when you do not understand. Show and tell about your toys or family. Practice speaking at home.
Class activity:
Let's have show and tell time. Each pupil will bring something to show.
Evaluation questions:
How do you ask a question?
What should you do when speaking?
What would you like to show and tell?
Summary:
Speaking up helps us learn and share.

topics.title: Handling mistakes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain that mistakes help learning.
The pupils should be able to fix a mistake.
Introduction:
Everyone makes mistakes. It is part of learning.
Content:
Mistakes are not bad. They teach us to try again. If you spill water, wipe it up. If you write wrong, erase it. Say sorry when you make mistakes. Learn from every mistake.
Class activity:
Let's play 'Fix it'. I will pretend to make mistakes and pupils will show how to fix them.
Evaluation questions:
What should you do when you make a mistake?
Why are mistakes not bad?
How do you learn from mistakes?
Summary:
Mistakes help us grow and become better.

topics.title: Friendship skills
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a new friend.
The pupils should be able to solve a friend problem.
Introduction:
Friends make school fun. We need to learn how to be good friends.
Content:
Share your toys. Take turns. Say please and thank you. Help friends when they fall. If friends fight, talk and solve it. Be kind every day.
Class activity:
Let's practice making friends. Pupils will walk around and greet each other nicely.
Evaluation questions:
How do you make a new friend?
What should you do if friends fight?
Why is sharing important?
Summary:
Good friends make school happy.

topics.title: Gratitude letters
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write a thank you letter.
The pupils should be able to deliver a letter with a smile.
Introduction:
Teachers help us learn. We should say thank you.
Content:
Write your teacher's name. Draw a picture. Write thank you. Tell what you like about school. Give the letter with a smile. Say thank you with your voice too.
Class activity:
Let's write thank you letters to our teachers.
Evaluation questions:
What do you write in a thank you letter?
How do you give a letter nicely?
Who should we thank at school?
Summary:
Thank you letters make teachers happy.

topics.title: Memories book
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a memory page.
The pupils should be able to sign a friend's book.
Introduction:
We have had fun in nursery school. Let's remember our good times.
Content:
Put pictures of your class. Draw your classroom. Write your name. Sign your friends' pages. Add a favorite memory. Keep the book forever.
Class activity:
Let's make a memories book for our class.
Evaluation questions:
What should you put in your memory page?
How do you sign a friend's book?
Why is a memories book special?
Summary:
Our memories book will help us remember nursery school.

topics.title: Revision and send off
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state something they learned.
The pupils should be able to say goodbye nicely.
Introduction:
We have grown so much in nursery school. It is time to celebrate.
Content:
We learned to read and write. We made good friends. We learned to be kind. We learned to share. We learned to take care of ourselves. Now we are ready for primary school.
Class activity:
Let's have a graduation party. We will sing songs and say what we learned.
Evaluation questions:
What did you learn in nursery school?
Who will you miss most?
What are you excited for in primary school?
Summary:
We are ready for big school. Goodbye nursery, hello primary!
